rule: plan.md section 3: derive(b1, op) changes exactly one dimension; every event is shown / implied (with its cue) / omitted; outcome and speakers equal b1.
pinned_dimensions: material set (same FORAGED pieces at b1: page-cartoonist pieces + Bubley visitor)
handmade lettering (page/glyphs.json strokes; variants/glyphs_extra.json adds '2','F' in the same pen for the labels only)
1934 LoC sheet ground, hand-ruled ~9 px borders, cut-paper balloons, 8 px scissor margins, one down-right paper shadow
tonal rule: one levels curve per source photograph, no filters
outcome: key stays on its hook, SERVICE door stays closed, goal forgotten

E0.cue: clerk seated, memo '4:15 - open SERVICE door. Key in cupboard.' legible on the desk

E1.cue: P2 desk empty but for the memo, clerk rising out of the right edge; P3 clerk mid-step, SERVICE card on the closed door

E2.cue: soft visitor shape behind the TICKET OFFICE glass; 'What time is it?' tail exits the left edge through the window

E3.cue: clock at 4:10; 'Ten past four!' tail to the clerk's mouth

E3b.cue: empty window; 'Thanks!' tail exits the left edge (departure itself implied by that cue)

E4.cue: door open on its jamb, brass key on its hook with SERVICE tag

E5.cue: pencil to chin under 'What the hell was I looking for, anyway?'; key unmoved on its hook; SERVICE card on the closed door

B.outcome: goal not achieved; key on hook; SERVICE door closed

D1.label: Derivative 1 - Compressed (2 panels)

E0.cue: the same handmade memo slip, legible on the desk (bottom centre of C1)

E1.cue: clerk risen from his chair (P2's rising pose), behind the desk, his arm already out of C1's right edge: he is leaving

E2.cue: 'What time is it?' read first (top-left), tail exits C1's left edge through the TICKET OFFICE window; no visitor is seen

E3.cue: 'Ten past four!' stacked below/right of the question, tail to the clerk's mouth; the office clock on the wall reads 4:10

E3b.cue: small 'Thanks!' read first in C2 (top-left), tail exits C2's left edge; her leaving implied by that exit only

E4.cue: the arrival and the opening are not drawn as actions; C2 shows their result: door open on its jamb, key on its hook with SERVICE tag

E5.cue: pencil to chin under 'What the hell was I looking for, anyway?'; key unmoved at his elbow; SERVICE card on the closed door

speakers_check.What time is it?: VISITOR (tail off-panel left, not to the clerk: the counterexample 'tail to his own mouth' is avoided)

D1.outcome: unchanged: key on hook in C2, SERVICE door closed
declared_losses: P3's walk past the closed SERVICE door is gone; the route from desk to cupboard is carried only by the cut between C1 and C2
the visitor is never seen (no soft figure behind glass): she exists only as two tails from the left edge

time between beats is carried by balloon reading order inside each panel: in C2 'Thanks!' is read before the forgetting line, so in the still the thanks seems to reach him at the cupboard (b1 puts E3b before E4); the film keeps the order by landing 'Thanks!' first, then the forgetting balloon
E4 is shown only as its result state (door already open)
C1 inherits the b1 office plate's inpainting smear at the desk edge left of the memo (plate defect noted by the test-shot review, owned by cutout-surgeon/page-cartoonist)

D2.label: Derivative 2 - From the platform
D2.changed_dimension: viewpoint (outside the ticket window, the VISITOR's side)

E0.cue: the memo lies on the desk in V2 but is only a few millimetres tall through the glass and cannot be read: the motive is not recoverable from this page

E1.cue: through the glass the desk is already empty when we first see it (E1 happened out of view)

E2.cue: V1: she stands at the station window (counter bell is film sound only); V2: 'What time is it?' with its tail out of the panel's bottom edge, to the viewpoint, i.e. to her

E3.cue: the clerk seen through the glass under the neon, clock at 4:10 beside him, 'Ten past four!' tail to his mouth through the glass

E3b.cue: V3 'Thanks!' tail out of the bottom edge (hers); V4 is V1's camera again: her place at the window is empty and she is cut by the left edge, pitched into a step, leaving

E4.cue: far back through the glass the cupboard door stands open on its jamb; his arrival and the opening are not seen

E5.cue: far back: the clerk before the open cupboard, pencil at his temple (scratching his head: the Rothstein source pose), the key a small glint still on its hook, SERVICE card on the still-closed door. His line is NOT on this page: from the platform it is not heard, so the forgetting is carried by the gesture alone

speakers_check.What time is it?: VISITOR (tail to the viewpoint, off-panel bottom)

D2.outcome: unchanged: key still on its hook (V4), SERVICE door closed with its card (V1, V4); nobody opens it. The counterexample 'visitor sees him take the key and open the door' is avoided.
declared_losses: the memo and so the motive are unrecoverable (E0 omitted)
the forgetting line is unheard; E5 rests on the head-scratch gesture and the unmoved key
his walk, the opening of the cupboard and the departure are all out of view or implied

the clerk keeps his photographed head angle (eyes down) in V3 rather than a turned head: no second photograph of the agent exists and the test-shot notes forbid a 2D roll; the turn is a -6 deg hinge on the collar only

the station front is a different FSA/OWI station (Bubley 1943, Cincinnati vicinity) joined by collage to the Rothstein 1937 office; its NISER ICE CREAM neon stays on the glass as found (the BUS STATION board and the advertising posters are cropped out)

the visitor is only seen frontally (the only plate of her); in V4 she leaves by the left edge of a repeated camera rather than small and far along a platform: no open-licence wide platform plate of this station was found

deviation from plan.md section 5 (D2 V4 'the key cannot be seen'): the key is left as a small visible glint on its hook, because hiding it would leave the unchanged outcome unreadable from this page (B2 asks readers to see the same outcome); recorded here, not a change to the frozen bar

through_glass_method: V1-V4: an optical composite of real plates: the office interior (Rothstein pieces, laid as in b1) x transmission t + the Bubley window's own pixels (reflections, display plants) x (1-t), t falling down the pane (V1/V4 0.62->0.40 far back, V2 0.80->0.52, V3 0.84->0.62); the neon sign's tubes and card are the window's own pixels re-laid in front. No blur, grain or filter added.

tone_measured.bar_supporting_measure: >=35% page px L>220 and >=8% L<40: D1 and D2 both meet it

rest_identity.note: variants/rest/<D1|D2>/<panel>/layers.json recomposed vs page crop (mean abs, 0-255)
